## Agent definition

# Legacy Calc Reproduction

## Role
Reproduces existing project calcs in the licensed native programs, case by case, before anyone revises them. A
reproduction counts only when a native file was computed and saved and its results were compared to the source
values. Works in its own context with a continuation checklist; a job typically takes 6-10 h of agent time. Updates to
current plans and redlines happen only after reproduction.

Licensed set (D16, default to confirm): FHWA Hydraulic Toolbox, HY-8, Civil 3D hydraulic tools (Hydraflow), HEC-RAS,
HEC-HMS, FLO-2D, PC-Hydro. FlowMaster and CulvertMaster are legacy: their files are sources to reproduce, not tools
to run. HY-8 is a supervised step by default; .hy8 files are written only from a template saved by HY-8 itself;
unattended HY-8 only after the writer is validated on that machine (D10).

## Inputs
- Job number; scope (inlets, storm drain, culverts); EKOS job root (D56).
- Native sources: .fm8.sqlite, .cvm, .stm, .hy8, .hyd and the calc workbooks (signed-sealed, 100 pct, later versions).
- Plan sets (prior and latest) and redlines; pavement drainage maps; LandXML alignments for station/offset.
- Outfall data (inverts, receiving water levels).

## Outputs
In `20_Working\legacy_repro\` unless noted:
- `case_register.csv`: case ID, source file, source workbook and tab, inputs with provenance, scenario, version.
- `INPUT\`, `WORKING\`, `NATIVE\` file sets per program (INPUT never computed or overwritten).
- Native reports exported raw (PDF + text exports); compact one-page sheets built from saved native values.
- `comparison.xlsx` (formulas, not pasted values): source vs native per case at native precision, with differences.
- `native_file_index.csv` (native and editable file per case).
- `continuation_checklist.md` and `work_status_log.md` from `templates/`.
- Independent spreadsheet checks labelled preliminary, kept in 40_QC (D30).

## Tools
- UI automation on EKOS with screenshot-based targeting of modal dialogs (no CLI or API in these programs).
- Civil 3D on EKOS (Hydraflow launched from inside Civil 3D).
- Shell on EKOS for parsing exports, workbook formula reading, hashing; Python by full path (D11).
- File read on sources; file write in 20_Working\legacy_repro and 40_QC.
- MCP library server (`get_skill`, `get_qc_rules`, `log_lesson`) or `library_cli.py`.

## Skills it calls
| Skill | Used for |
|---|---|
| hy8-native-runs | culvert reproduction: template-based .hy8, session hygiene, report export, HDS-5 check |
| swmm-ssa-storm-drain | independent storm drain check where a second basis is wanted (40_QC only) |
| cad-base-update | LandXML alignments for station/offset locations |
| drainage-report-standard | folder layout, native-output appendix rules (D38) |
| drainage-report-build | appendix and table rules when reproduced cases feed a report |

## Procedure
1. Inventory native sources and workbook tabs; register each case input with provenance in `case_register.csv`.
   Reproduce the signed-sealed workbook and later workbooks separately; confirm which copy is current.
2. Read bypass links from workbook formulas (not only the summary sheet); build the bypass graph and get the run order
   with `scripts/bypass_order.py inlets.csv --out run_order.csv`. Approach flow = local runoff plus upstream bypass
   only; confined pairs: full flow to the first inlet, bypass plus verified local to the next.
3. Inlets (FHWA Hydraulic Toolbox 5.5):
   a. Write a generated INPUT .hyd (CURBCALC blocks) and keep it uncomputed.
   b. Clear the project with New / No before loading another file.
   c. Open each calculation, click Compute / Compute Inlet Data, OK; Save As a separate NATIVE .hyd. Never save
      computed results over the INPUT file.
   d. Enter values by individual key presses or single-value paste; Tab commits but does not refresh results -
      click Compute.
   e. Run inlets in bypass order; after each, enter captured and bypass flows in the CSV and run
      `bypass_order.py inlets.csv --check` so flow balance holds at each node through to pipes or channels.
4. Storm drain (Hydraflow Storm Sewers): launch from inside Civil 3D; copy the .stm and zero result fields in the
   working input; compute, save, print Inventory / Summary / HGL to PDF and export the Summary grid to text; diff source
   vs native line by line; record outfall tailwater per line; never substitute earlier tailwaters without evidence.
5. Culverts: per hy8-native-runs (supervised; template-based .hy8; kill HY864.exe before start; empty project before
   open; save before export; reopen NATIVE in a fresh project to confirm inputs).
6. Parse saved native results and compare with source values at native precision in `comparison.xlsx`; report invalid
   results (e.g. -nan capture) as INVALID, never zero; never invent geometry.
7. Export native reports raw; build compact one-page sheets from saved native values, labelled "extracted summary" in
   any appendix (D38); record source, scenario, version, inputs, run date and differences per case.
8. Only after reproduction: copy cases and update per current plans and redlines. Label superseded working copies
   VOID_ only when a verified replacement exists. Keep independent spreadsheet checks labelled preliminary in 40_QC.
9. Keep the continuation checklist and work status log current every hour of work. Do not touch HEC-RAS when the
   scope is inlets, culverts and storm drain.
10. Hand the comparison workbook, native file index and difference list to report-writer and qc-reviewer.

## Gotchas
- Bulk text entry into a numeric field did not change it; individual key presses or single-value paste worked
  (VALENCIA-001).
- Tab commits a value but does not refresh results; click Compute or the results are stale (VALENCIA-001).
- A file that loads with changed inputs is not a run; only a computed and saved native file counts (VALENCIA-001).
- Clear the project with New/No before loading another; never save computed results over the INPUT file
  (VALENCIA-001).
- Zero local-depression width returned -nan(ind) capture (element 207); report INVALID, never zero, and do not invent
  geometry (VALENCIA-001).
- Native orifice results matched g = 32.16 ft/s2 with Cd 0.67; an independent check using 32.2 differs slightly, so
  report the native values (VALENCIA-001).
- No CLI or API: launching with a filename argument did not load inputs; UI automation needs screenshot-based
  targeting of modal dialogs (VALENCIA-001).
- On reopen the Summary flow shows 0.00 and COMPUTE appears; reopening is not a rerun (VALENCIA-004).
- The program warns flow/area/C missing when Known Q is used; record it and reconcile the intended Known Q method
  (VALENCIA-004).
- The printed PDF is image-only; keep the Summary text export for values or OCR the PDF (VALENCIA-004).
- Inherited outlet tailwaters were much higher than outfall inverts (e.g. 2504.42 vs 2472.59 ft); flag, do not zero
  all tailwaters (VALENCIA-004).
- Three generated V1-V3 inputs failed before V4; keep them as VOID_ (VALENCIA-004).
- A run takes 6-10 h of agent time; it needs its own context and a written continuation checklist and status log
  (VALENCIA-005).
- The signed-sealed revision workbook and the 100 pct workbook differ; reproduce each separately (VALENCIA-005).
- Saved values in a source file are not a rerun (VALENCIA-005).
- Do not touch HEC-RAS when the scope is inlets, culverts and storm drain (VALENCIA-005).
- The first 72 native runs missed bypass links found later in workbook J/K formulas; all were VOIDed and rerun
  (VALENCIA-013).
- Duplicating full flow at a downstream inlet overstated Q; use bypass only (VALENCIA-013).
- A from-scratch .hy8 writer gave wrong catalog codes and units (arch dims saved in ft while the UI shows in); 8 arch
  runs were VOIDed; take codes and enums from an HY-8-saved template (VALENCIA-003, D10).

## Stop conditions
- A source value cannot be reproduced after inputs are checked against the source file: record the difference, do not
  adjust inputs to force a match, and ask JCO.
- Native result invalid (-nan, missing geometry): report INVALID and stop that case.
- Internal plan or workbook conflict (two values for one feature): record both; do not pick; escalate.
- HY-8 closes without a report: failed run; retry one crossing at a time; stop after two failures and escalate.
- Scope creep into HEC-RAS or redesign before reproduction is complete: stop and ask.

## Escalation (to JCO)
- Differences between native and source values beyond native rounding, with both values and the input evidence.
- Which workbook copy governs (signed-sealed vs later) when they differ.
- Tailwater basis at outfalls; Known Q method choices; plan conflicts found during reproduction.
- Any design change implied by current plans (handled after reproduction, through the decision register).

## Learning log
End every run with `log_lesson(project='<job no>', text='<UI or file behavior, the workaround, how it was verified>',
evidence=['<NATIVE file or comparison.xlsx>'], source_ai='<platform>')`, or on EKOS:
`D:\EKOS\Library\09_Server\.venv\Scripts\python.exe D:\EKOS\Library\09_Server\library_cli.py log-lesson --project <job no> --source-ai <platform> --text "..." --evidence "<path>"`.

## Change log
- 1.0.0 2026-10-22: built from cluster HYD-C21 (with HY-8 rules from HYD-C20); decisions D10, D16, D30, D38, D56.
  Added scripts/bypass_order.py (tested on sample inlet chains, cycle and unknown-target cases). Items marked
  "default, to confirm": D16 (FlowMaster and CulvertMaster treated as legacy, not licensed).

## Skill: hy8-native-runs v1.0.0

# HY-8 Native Runs

## When to use
- A report, memo or appendix needs HY-8 native culvert output.
- Reproducing a CulvertMaster (legacy, decision D16) or archived HY-8 case natively.
- Contractor substitution check (e.g. boxes to arches) against the approved report headwater.
- User-defined arch or irregular shapes.
- HY-8 rating tables for FLO-2D structures (flo2d-model-runs Step 4) or HEC-RAS crossing checks.

Licensed set (decision D16, default, to confirm): HY-8 and the FHWA Hydraulic Toolbox are the culvert tools;
CulvertMaster and FlowMaster are legacy and used only to read archived files.

## Inputs
- Plan profile stations / elevations or survey for barrel count, size, length, inverts (not callout text).
- Design discharges (and the sensitivity flows the jurisdiction requires), tailwater basis, roadway profile.
- The approved analysis for the crossing, if one exists, and the current plan shape.
- Seed / template .hy8 saved by HY-8 itself for each culvert type and material in use (library resource or
  a project seed; never a file written from scratch).

Scripts (hydraulics env by full path; `<PY>` = `"%HYDRAULICS_PY%"` = `C:\EKOS\hydraulics\.venv\Scripts\python.exe`, per
08_Platform_Builds/ENVIRONMENTS.md):
- `scripts/hy8_template.py` - `fill` (values into a template by exact key), `check` (CRLF, ENDPROJECTFILE,
  keys, inch/ft warning), `diff` (INPUT vs NATIVE).
- `scripts/hds5_check.py` - independent HDS-5 inlet / outlet control check (internal QC only).

Run mode (decision D10): HY-8 is a supervised step by default - a person (or the supervisor with a visible
desktop) watches the GUI session. Unattended runs only after the template writer and the export sequence are
validated on that machine and the validation is logged.

## Steps

### 1. Confirm the crossing data
1. Take barrel count, size, length and inverts from plan profile stations / elevations or survey. Confirm the
   approved analysis matches the current plan shape (e.g. boxes vs arches). On any conflict ask JCO.
2. If no baseline exists, rebuild one with stated assumptions.
3. Read request wording carefully (e.g. "drainage area reduction" may mean opening area per cell).
4. HY-8 cannot model a skewed box inlet (e.g. 25 deg); note the limitation in the report.

### 2. Independent check first (internal)
1. `<PY> hds5_check.py --shape box --span 10 --rise 4 --barrels 3 --length 120 --slope 0.010 --n 0.012
   --ke 0.5 --inlet box_90_15_wingwall --tw 3.2 --q 250 450`. Save the JSON in 40_QC (decision D30); never
   put it in a deliverable.
2. This check is the reconciliation target for Step 6.

### 3. Write the INPUT .hy8 from a template
1. Start from a template saved by HY-8 itself. Take catalog codes (e.g. IRREGSIZE) and material enums from the
   native example; never infer them (e.g. from a RAS HDF).
2. Barrel data and geometry are serialized in ft even when the UI shows inches.
3. Match exact field keys with whitespace boundaries (INLETEDGETYPE is not INLETEDGETYPE71).
4. `<PY> hy8_template.py fill <seed.hy8> <values.json> INPUT_<crossing>.hy8`, then
   `<PY> hy8_template.py check <seed.hy8> INPUT_<crossing>.hy8` (CRLF, ENDPROJECTFILE, no invented keys,
   inch/ft warning). For repeats, edit a seed crossing rather than building from nothing.
5. User-defined arches: solve springline and tangent point from crown / haunch radius, span and rise;
   integrate the exact area; about 19 coordinate pairs within 0.3 pct of the area; save the coordinates JSON
   beside the model; note that inlet relationships for user shapes are generic (no manufacturer inlet data).
6. Keep the writer as an importable library module; never exec source text borrowed from another project.

### 4. Supervised HY-8 session
1. Kill any HY864.exe before each start.
2. File New (Ctrl+N, answer No) to an empty project before Open. Opening into a non-empty project appends the
   crossings to the current tree.
3. Open INPUT; confirm only the intended crossings are loaded. Never save a contaminated session.
4. Check every tab: tailwater type, roadway crest, inlet edge, n, material, barrel dimensions as displayed.
5. Run Analysis. Save the project as NATIVE_<crossing>.hy8 BEFORE exporting (HY-8 can close during export).
6. Create Report (Shift+End selects all crossings) to Word, then PDF. If export closes HY-8 without a DOCX,
   the run failed: retry one crossing at a time.
7. Reopen NATIVE in a fresh project and confirm inputs; `<PY> hy8_template.py diff INPUT_<x>.hy8 NATIVE_<x>.hy8`
   to see what HY-8 changed.
8. Keep INPUT, WORKING and NATIVE files. Word locks an open export DOCX; if a rename fails, write a VOID
   sidecar note instead.
9. Supervised automation notes: refresh the screenshot before every action (focus and cached modal indexes go
   stale); run button invokes on threads because dialogs block; on the welcome screen Return opens the
   chooser, Alt+N moves to the file name, verify the caret before typing.

### 5. Read the native report
1. Parse the exported report: total = barrel flow + roadway flow.
2. Record the solver mode actually used (e.g. Full Flow); do not call it a matched RAS profile comparison
   unless the mode matches.
3. Check cover for each alternative against the road profile.
4. For archived cases, compare printed inputs with the saved model before calling a mismatch.

### 6. Reconcile
1. Stop and reconcile if native and independent results differ by more than 0.2 ft HW or 0.5 fps.
2. Compare with archived output field by field and keep the differences; never adjust inputs to force a match.

### 7. Substitution checks (contractor alternatives)
1. Identical flow, slope, n, length and fixed tailwater from the report model.
2. Bracket the entrance loss (Ke 0.2 beveled, 0.5 square edge).
3. Stress cases: high tailwater, and full crossing flow through one structure where the original flow split
   between openings.
4. Compare HW with the report existing HW; report differences in computed area loss (e.g. recomputed vs
   contractor value).
5. One-page memo with native output attached (drainage-technical-memo).

### 8. Barrel-only checks
1. An artificial high road crest suppresses overtopping and does not prove zero overflow; state it.

### 9. Deliverable
1. Native report PDF of the selected design goes in the appendix (decision D38); option tables only while
   options are open, each with its calc sheet.
2. Project datum inverts, not an arbitrary datum; print areas so each sheet is one page.

## Jurisdiction add-ons
Load with `get_skill("hy8-native-runs", resource="addons/<file>.md")`:
- `addons/caltrans-california.md` - HDM Table 808.1 alternatives and sensitivity flow list.
- `addons/city-of-tucson.md` - contractor substitution memo against the approved report HW.

## Gotchas
- Opening a file into a non-empty HY-8 project appends its crossings to the current tree (e.g. into a prior benchmark session), producing a combined model; never save a contaminated session (CAMPBELL-013, EKOS-LOCAL-012, VALENCIA-003)
- HY-8 closing during report export without producing a DOCX is a failed run; retry one crossing at a time (CAMPBELL-013, EKOS-LOCAL-012)
- The .hy8 writer was borrowed from another project by exec of split source text with a hard path; keep it as an importable library module (CALFIRE-012)
- HY-8 has no command-line report; GUI automation took 9 probe scripts and about 25 min; kill HY864.exe before each start and invoke run buttons on threads because dialogs block (CALFIRE-012)
- Barrel dimensions are stored in ft even if the UI shows in (CAMPBELL-013)
- HY-8 cannot model 25 deg skew on a box inlet; note it (CAMPBELL-013)
- An agent team left HY-8 pending; native runs happened 11 days later; schedule HY-8 as an explicit supervised step (CAMPBELL-013)
- Accessibility focus and cached modal element indexes went stale; refresh the screenshot before every action (EKOS-LOCAL-012)
- Native summary showed Full Flow mode despite the profile toolbar; do not call it a matched RAS profile comparison (EKOS-LOCAL-012)
- An unattended local HY-8 run was never achieved; only supervised GUI runs worked (EKOS-LOCAL-012)
- Recurrence: 2 modal failures and 2 key-matching failures (INLETEDGETYPE vs INLETEDGETYPE71) in one job (EKOS-LOCAL-012)
- Arch dimensions show in inches in the UI but BARRELDATA / BARRELGEOMETRY are saved in feet; the first 8 concrete-arch runs were wrong and voided (VALENCIA-003)
- A corrugated steel arch 50x31 in needed IRREGSIZE 1 1 1, not the code derived from the HDF; the report run closed HY-8 with no output until fixed (VALENCIA-003)
- Material enum was set wrong in a generated file (4 instead of concrete 1); corrected in the UI before the run (VALENCIA-003)
- The HY-8 window disappeared during Word export before the post-analysis save; save the project before exporting (VALENCIA-003)
- An archive printed 4.0 ft rise while the saved model had 3.5 ft; check printed inputs vs the saved model before calling a mismatch (VALENCIA-003)
- Word locks an open export DOCX; rename fails until closed, so use a VOID sidecar note (VALENCIA-003)
- The report analyzed six 12x8 ft boxes while the later plan shows three 24x8 ft arches, and the plan HW note repeated the old box result (SILVERBELL-014)
- A request said drainage area reduction; it meant opening area per cell (about 10 sq ft each, 29-30 sq ft total) (SILVERBELL-014)
- The original flow split between two openings; also test full crossing flow through one structure (SILVERBELL-014)
- Recomputed arch area loss (10.00 sq ft) differed from the contractor value (9.58); report the difference (SILVERBELL-014)
- Result was HW rise 0.45-0.50 ft, still at least 2.6 ft below existing HW; state margin to the approved HW (SILVERBELL-014)
- GUI automation through dialogs was slow and fragile; text editing of a seed .hy8 file was faster (SILVERBELL-015)
- Inlet relationships for user-defined shapes are generic; note no manufacturer inlet data (SILVERBELL-015)
- LibreOffice was not available for DOCX rendering; Word export was used for page QA (SILVERBELL-015)
- 72 in RCP alternative had under 1 ft cover; check cover for every alternative (CALFIRE-012)

## QC checks
- Pull: `get_qc_rules('culverts')`, `get_qc_rules('appendix')`.
- `hy8_template.py check` pass on every INPUT file; NATIVE reopened in a fresh project.
- HY-8 closed without a report = failed run, logged.
- Native vs independent HDS-5 within 0.2 ft HW and 0.5 fps, or the difference reconciled and recorded in 40_QC.
- Total flow = barrel + roadway; solver mode recorded; cover checked.
- Appendix carries the native report for the selected design; independent check not in the deliverable.

## Skill: swmm-ssa-storm-drain v1.0.0

# SWMM / SSA Storm Drain

## When to use
- Storage, peak control or HGL must be shown with a hydrograph model while the agency peak method is
  rational-type (e.g. Placer County Small Watershed) - Placer County CA add-on.
- Scripted SWMM models must be handed to an engineer in Autodesk SSA.
- An independent check of a storm drain HGL or a detention routing in an Arizona jurisdiction, where
  PC-Hydro / HEC-HMS and the agency-accepted tools stay primary (decision D26).
- A storm drain ties into a public main or street structure and HGL freeboard is checked.

Role by jurisdiction (decision D26):
| Jurisdiction | SWMM / SSA role |
|---|---|
| Arizona (Pima County RFCD, City of Tucson, Marana, Sahuarita, others) | independent check only; file in 40_QC (decision D30) unless JCO decides otherwise |
| Placer County CA (and other jurisdictions whose add-on allows it) | primary hydrograph / HGL model, calibrated to the county peak method |

## Inputs
- Agency target peaks per drainage area and design storm (county method calc; for Placer see
  drainage-report-build `addons/placer-county-ca.md` and this skill's add-on).
- Agency infiltration rate table, site plan areas (impervious, pervious, roof), pipe / structure data from
  survey or plans, storage / gallery / trench geometry.
- Receiving structure rim, invert and HGL from the agency or as-builts.

Scripts (hydro env interpreter by full path, D11; `<PY>` = `"%HYDRO_PY%"` = `C:\EKOS\hydrology\.venv\Scripts\python.exe`, per
the path in the 08_Platform_Builds/ENVIRONMENTS.md):
- `scripts/swmm_width_calibrate.py` - log-space bisection of subcatchment width to target peaks; geometric mean;
  fit report.

## Steps

### 1. Targets
1. Compute target peaks per area for each design storm with the county method; record the method and table
   values used.
2. Calibrate pre-condition (existing) catchments separately with their own targets.

### 2. Runoff-only calibration models
1. One runoff-only .inp per storm: each subcatchment to an outfall; constant-rate infiltration (Horton
   f0 = fc = agency table rate, decay 0); no depression storage; REPORT_STEP 1 min or less.
2. `<PY> swmm_width_calibrate.py --sub <S> --case <runoff_10yr.inp> <Q10> --case <runoff_25yr.inp> <Q25>
   --case <runoff_100yr.inp> <Q100>`. It bisects width in log space (26 iterations default) per storm, takes
   the geometric mean of the storm widths, and reports the fit of that one width against every target
   (pass within 10 pct).
3. Report the fit in the memo (target vs modeled per storm). Plot a calibration figure.
4. Carry the calibrated widths unchanged into every routed scenario.
5. Do not try to close the gap by switching SSA hydrology methods (TR-55 / TR-20); width calibration is what
   matches the county peaks.

### 3. Routed models
1. Write .inp in SWMM 5.1 syntax (SSA imports 5.1), one file per scenario named
   `<code>-<side>-<run>-<storm>-<condition>`.
2. Keep routing Hydrodynamic. Set surcharge elevation and sag-inlet ponded area deliberately (otherwise SSA
   raises Warning 108 surcharge elevation below max depth, and Warning 139 zero ponded area on sag inlets).
3. Storage nodes: exfiltration rates from the agency / geotech basis; record the source.

### 4. Tailwater and receiving system
1. Get rim, invert and HGL of the receiving structure from the agency or as-builts.
2. Run a fixed-tailwater case and a free-outfall case; report both. The model and the memo state the same
   boundary.
3. Compare the assumed tailwater with the lowest onsite rims and gallery crowns before any site runoff arrives.
4. Compare proposed peaks with receiving storm drain capacity and HGL; explain why each discharge alternative
   (alley, street, storm drain, retention) was or was not used; coordinate connection feasibility with the
   site designer.
5. Verify report claims (e.g. impervious area removed) against the site plan.

### 5. SSA handoff
1. Import in SSA: File > Import > EPA SWMM v5.x. Save each scenario as .spf with its text report.
2. SSA does not transfer storage exfiltration: set storage-node exfiltration in Project Options and re-enter
   gallery / trench infiltration rates by hand. Recheck surcharge elevations and sag-inlet ponded areas.
3. Keep Hydrodynamic routing in SSA.

### 6. Compare and report
1. Parse the SSA .rpt (Node Depth Summary, Outfall Loading, Storage Node Summary, continuity) and the SWMM .rpt
   on identical inputs; compare HGL and outfall peaks.
2. SSA routing continuity omits exfiltrated volume; report continuity with exfiltration added back.
3. SSA uses the older SWMM 5.1 surcharge algorithm; where surcharged node depths differ, use the more
   conservative result and say which engine it came from.
4. HGL freeboard against the governing criterion at every structure (Placer: 0.5 ft below rim).
5. Native program output in the appendix (decision D38): SSA / SWMM report pages for the selected design.

## Jurisdiction add-ons
- `addons/placer-county-ca.md` (load with `get_skill("swmm-ssa-storm-drain", resource="addons/placer-county-ca.md")`):
  SWMM / SSA as primary, Small Watershed targets, Table 5-3 infiltration, 0.5 ft HGL freeboard, East Placer
  items.
- City of Tucson: justify retention vs discharge with receiving storm drain capacity and HGL; rules in
  drainage-report-build `addons/city-of-tucson.md` (TANGERINE-025).

## Gotchas
- Switching SSA hydrology between TR-55 and TR-20 never matched county peaks (50-yr 0.13 vs 0.90 cfs); calibration of width closes the gap (HOMEWOOD-003)
- Calibrate the pre-condition catchment separately with its own target (HOMEWOOD-003)
- SSA does not transfer storage exfiltration on import; peak-control and WQ runs were wrong until set by hand (HOMEWOOD-004)
- SSA routing continuity omits exfiltrated volume, so a run shows 19-48 pct continuity error equal to exfiltration; report it with exfiltration added back (HOMEWOOD-004)
- SSA uses the older SWMM 5.1 surcharge algorithm; surcharged nodes ran 0.3-2.1 ft higher than SWMM 5.2; use the more conservative result (HOMEWOOD-004)
- The original SSA export raised Warning 108 (surcharge elevation below max) and 139 (zero ponded area on sag inlets); set these deliberately (HOMEWOOD-004)
- Tailwater set 6 in below the receiving grate was only 0.52-0.55 ft below the lowest onsite rims, so the lower system failed the 0.5 ft criterion before site runoff arrived; free outfall passed (HOMEWOOD-010)
- The original model used a free outfall while the memo claimed tailwater; model and memo must state the same boundary (HOMEWOOD-010)
- A draft asserted retention without checking the storm drain and claimed impervious removal the plan did not show (TANGERINE-025)
- The .rpt Subcatchment Runoff Summary rounds small peaks to 0.01 cfs; the calibration script reads the binary output instead (build note, 2026-10-22)

## QC checks
- Pull: `get_qc_rules('storm-drain')`; Placer: `get_qc_rules('placer')`.
- width_calibration.json pass (each storm within 10 pct with the single geometric-mean width); pre and post
  calibrated separately.
- Exfiltration re-entered in SSA; continuity reported with exfiltration added back.
- Fixed-tailwater and free-outfall cases both run; memo boundary matches the model.
- HGL freeboard checked at every structure; more conservative engine result used where they differ.
- Arizona jobs: SWMM files and results in 40_QC only, not in the deliverable (D26, D30).

## Change log
- 1.0.0 2026-10-22: built from clusters HYD-C22 and HYD-C23; decisions D26, D30, D38. Width calibration script
  tested against the SWMM 5.2.4 engine (swmm-toolkit) on a synthetic catchment.

## Skill: cad-base-update v1.0.0

# CAD Base Update and Civil 3D Automation

## When to use
- A consultant base (architect building/site plan, survey, civil) is reissued and xrefs must be swapped.
- A script or agent needs alignments, profiles, corridors or surfaces out of Civil 3D, or must load .NET helpers into a running session.
- Only a PDF DCR and GIS linework exist and a native Civil 3D base, corridor and plan set is needed.
- Site or model geometry produced outside CAD (Python, QGIS, model grids) must go to Civil 3D users.

Part A (reissue) is the most frequent use. Parts B-D are run as needed. Every part follows the source-file rule in Step 0.

## Inputs
- Job number and the Standard v0.3 job folder (D56): received bases land in `01_Reference\By_Others\<consultant>\`; working copies and scratch exports in `20_Working\<Initials>_<YYYYMMDD>_<Topic>\`.
- The CAD project xref folder (where the live xrefs sit) and the current check-plot set.
- Exhibit and sheet register (which exhibits/sheets reference which xref).
- For Part D: model grid or surface, CRS and vertical datum from the project data log.
- Environment: EKOS Python environment interpreter by full path (D11); no .ps1 files (D12).

## Steps

### Step 0 - Source files are read-only (all parts)
1. Copy every source DWG/DXF/LandXML to a scratch folder under `20_Working\...` and run all automated reads there. (NORTHLOOP-018)
2. Write a SHA-256 manifest of the source folder before the run and compare after; stop and report if any source file changed:
   `"%DOCS_PY%" <skill>\scripts\hash_manifest.py make <source_folder> <scratch>\before.json`
   then `... hash_manifest.py check <source_folder> <scratch>\before.json` (exit code 1 = a source file changed or vanished).
3. Never open a received DWG in place with accoreconsole or a script that saves; console runs can refresh the DWG and its .bak. (NORTHLOOP-018)

### Part A - Consultant base reissue
1. Log the reissue: consultant, issue date, file names, transmittal reference, in the reissue log beside the xref folder (`CAD_Reissue_Log.md`, one row per issue).
2. Before replacing any xref, copy the current xref set to `<xref folder>\<consultant>\Archive\<YYYYMMDD>_Before_CAD_Update\`. Do not overwrite an earlier archive folder. (HOMEWOOD-021)
3. Place the new files in `01_Reference\By_Others\<consultant>\<YYYYMMDD>\` as received (unchanged), then copy into the xref folder under the same xref names so host drawings repath without edits.
4. Check the new base before swapping: units, insertion base point, CRS/known points against the previous issue (at least 3 points); flag any shift. (STARVALLEY-014; see project-intake for the full CRS check)
5. Swap/reload the xrefs, then list what moved: buildings and footprints, pads and finished floors, site linework, walls, utilities and electrical areas, grading limits. Use an overlay of old vs new (old in a contrasting color) or a scripted DXF comparison of layer extents and entity counts. (HOMEWOOD-021)
6. Flag affected design items: storm drain alignments and inverts, inlets, grading and FG surfaces, galleries/underground storage, basin footprints, drainage-area boundaries, exhibits and report figures. (HOMEWOOD-021)
7. Write the change list `CAD_Change_List_<YYYYMMDD>.md` beside the archive folder: what moved, affected items, affected sheets/exhibits (register IDs), rework owner, status. (HOMEWOOD-021)
8. Reissue check plots for every affected sheet/exhibit; mark superseded figures per the exhibit register (move old record figures to `10_Record\_Superseded\X\`, never delete).
9. If the reissue changes impervious area, drainage areas or facility footprints, notify the hydrology/hydraulics owner and add an open item to the QC open-items document (D44).

### Part B - Civil 3D automation (helpers, accoreconsole, COM)
1. Before scheduling, confirm a Civil 3D seat is free on this machine (no "Device limit reached"); if not, stop and report rather than queue. (TANGERINE-010)
2. Build any NETLOAD plugin as a proper project targeting the installed AutoCAD .NET runtime (one runtime only); test it in accoreconsole on one scratch drawing before any batch. (TANGERINE-010)
3. Pre-trust one helper folder, or batch helpers into one DLL, so the user approves the Load Once / trust dialog once. (SILVERBELL-009)
4. Verify the exact target drawing FullName before each SendCommand; re-check after any ActiveDocument change. (SILVERBELL-009)
5. Write a completion marker file per helper (`<helper>.done` with time and drawing); never repeat NETLOAD for a helper already logged complete. On restart, read the markers and resume. (SILVERBELL-009)
6. Run native CAD COM from an elevated shell; launch through Python (subprocess / win32com) or inline commands, not .ps1 files (D12). (SILVERBELL-009)
7. Headless runs: `"C:\Program Files\Autodesk\AutoCAD 2026\accoreconsole.exe" /i <scratch.dwg> /s <script.scr> /l en-US`; judge success by the output file existing and the return code being 0, and read the console log for "Unknown command" or "Unable to load assembly". (RKN-011, TANGERINE-010)
8. Fallback when helpers or seats fail: export LandXML alignments and profiles from Civil 3D by hand and read them by script; record the fallback in the run log. (TANGERINE-010)
9. InfraWorks: build the base model (terrain, aerial) only after CRS and vertical units are verified; never present source-only aerial views as proposed-corridor renders; label each view with its geometry basis. (TANGERINE-010)

### Part C - Base reconstruction from PDF DCR and GIS linework
1. Extract the construction baseline from the PDF vector strokes; georeference to the supplied GIS linework; keep a CAD-to-plan station crosswalk table. (SILVERBELL-007)
2. Build the EG TIN from clipped lidar (lidar choice and DEM per D53/D54, logged); trace the proposed profile from the plotted line at about 5 ft spacing. (SILVERBELL-007)
3. Build corridor regions at the source transition stations; record every schematic assumption on a decisions sheet. (SILVERBELL-007)
4. Produce individual sheets plus a combined PDF; package each revision with checksums. (SILVERBELL-007)
5. Keep the .mms companion file beside each DWG and include it in every copy and package. (SILVERBELL-007)
6. State the vertical datum of the DCR; if unknown, label EG vs FG differences as indicative only, not earthwork depths. (SILVERBELL-007)

### Part D - LandXML / DXF / DWG handoff to Civil 3D users
1. Confirm CRS and units of the outgoing geometry match the receiving drawing (EPSG and realization from the data log, D55 for Pima County; intl ft vs US survey ft stated).
2. Write LandXML 1.2: EX and PR TIN surfaces (25-ft grid inside grading limits + 300 ft), road alignments with FG profiles, private streets, block and lot parcels. LandXML point order is northing, easting, elevation. (RKN-011, STARVALLEY-014)
3. Check EX and PR surface point counts equal the grid count before export. (RKN-011)
4. Write a layered DXF (AutoCAD 2018 format) with lot numbers and 2-ft/10-ft contours. (RKN-011)
5. Convert DXF to DWG with accoreconsole headless (Part B step 7); confirm the DWG exists and rc = 0. (RKN-011)
6. Open the DWG once in Civil 3D (or have the CAD user confirm) to see surfaces and alignments load; log the check.
7. Ship with a short transmittal note: CRS, vertical datum, units, surface extents, source model/plan and date.

## Gotchas
- Architect base was reissued about 7 times and the site plan 4 times in five months; each update forced storm drain and exhibit rework, so the archive and change list are not optional. (HOMEWOOD-021)
- AutoCAD console refreshed a historical DWG and its BAK; the DWG was restored from backup but the older BAK was lost. Work on scratch copies only. (NORTHLOOP-018)
- A csc-compiled Extract.dll mixing .NET 8 and .NET 10 references failed in accoreconsole with "Unable to load assembly", then "Unknown command". (TANGERINE-010)
- Civil 3D showed "Device limit reached" because another device held the seat; proposed corridor and six perspectives stayed pending. (TANGERINE-010)
- Choose Assembly and Load Once dialogs blocked COM; screen automation could not reach off-monitor dialogs and the user had to click for 4 helpers. (SILVERBELL-009)
- A generic assembly error left one helper unapplied; native grading finished only with a later helper. Check each helper's marker, not the batch exit. (SILVERBELL-009)
- Native CAD COM needs an elevated shell. (SILVERBELL-009)
- Recovered chainage drifted 32.7 ft over the corridor; keep the drift in the crosswalk, do not hide it with a coordinate shift. (SILVERBELL-007)
- Printed vertical-curve labels conflicted with the plotted line; the trace follows plotted geometry and the conflict is flagged on the decisions sheet. (SILVERBELL-007)
- DCR vertical datum unknown; EG vs FG differences are not earthwork depths. (SILVERBELL-007)
- Without the .mms companion file the large surface is lost. (SILVERBELL-007)
- LandXML declared EPSG:2223 but was in local site coordinates; check known points, not metadata. (STARVALLEY-014)
- Surface point counts that do not match the grid mean a clipped or duplicated export. (RKN-011)

## QC checks
- Pull rules: `get_qc_rules('crs')`, `get_qc_rules('exhibits')`, `get_qc_rules('existing-conditions')`.
- Before/after hash manifest filed for every automated CAD read; no source file changed.
- Each reissue has an archive folder, a reissue-log row and a change list naming affected sheets/exhibits; affected check plots reissued.
- Known-point check (3 points minimum) logged for each new base and each outgoing LandXML/DWG.
- Every helper has a completion marker; no helper applied twice; fallback use logged.
- Handoff: surface point counts = grid count; DWG exists and rc 0; opens with surfaces and alignments.
- Reconstruction: station crosswalk, decisions sheet, checksums per revision, .mms beside each DWG.

## Change log
- 1.0.0 2026-10-22: built from clusters DSO-C17, DSO-C21, DSO-C22, EXH-C14 (with DSO-C10 source-file rule and DSO-C05 known-point check); decisions D11, D12, D44, D53, D54, D55 (default, to confirm), D56. Archive folder name `<YYYYMMDD>_Before_CAD_Update` and reissue-log/change-list file names are defaults, to confirm.

## Skill: drainage-report-standard v0.4.0

# Drainage Report Standard (workbook -> assemble -> post-process -> Word export -> compiled PDF)

Skill version 0.4.0. The package code on EKOS is still v0.3.0: the v0.4 changes in `reference/v0.4_change_spec.md`
are a spec, implemented and regression-tested in Phase 5. Until then this skill runs the v0.3 package and uses the
library helpers in `scripts/` (recalc, post-process, Word export, compile) where v0.4 will add package steps.
Do not edit the package code from this skill.

## When to use
- A drainage report, TM, addendum, H&H study, TDN or DCR is built on the Standard workbook (any jurisdiction).
- Kickoff or re-scope of a report: folder, Kickoff sheet, coordination plan, register seeding.
- Promoting, superseding, reconciling or auditing calcs; a design flow or basis value changed.
- Regenerating a draft after a calc, plan or comment change; compiling the submittal PDF.
- Content and formatting rules come from `drainage-report-build` and `drainage-report-exhibit-standards`; this skill
  is the mechanics of the Standard package. Memos: `drainage-technical-memo`. Comment cycles:
  `agency-comment-response`. Handover zips: `delivery-package-build`. New project folder and data:
  `project-intake`.

## Inputs
- Package root (EKOS): `D:\LocalAI_Test\Drainage_Report_Standard_v0.3_TRANSFER\Drainage_Report_Standard_v0.3_TRANSFER`.
  `<STANDARD>` = `<root>\standard\30_Standard_v0.3`. Map of files: `reference/package_map.md`.
- `%DOCS_PY%` = full path of the EKOS documents venv interpreter (openpyxl, python-docx, lxml, pypdf, pywin32)
  (D11). Set on EKOS as a user variable: `DOCS_PY=C:\EKOS\documents\.venv\Scripts\python.exe` (08_Platform_Builds/ENVIRONMENTS.md).
  Never bare `python` or a global pip in a long job.
- `%SK%` = this skill's `scripts\` folder in the library.
- Job report folder `<Job>\ENGR\DOCS\Drainage Report\<ReportID>_<ShortName>\` and its workbook
  `00_Admin\<Job>_<ReportID>_Workbook.xlsx`.
- Stop and ask if missing: workbook path; milestone / revision / office address / contact in Setup (P-09..P-21);
  confirmed reviewing agency; JCO seal name and PE number (P-07/P-08).

## Steps

### A. Release check (every run)
1. Read `<STANDARD>\CURRENT.json`: `published: true`, note `standard_version`. On EKOS set `release_folder` to the
   EKOS path once (the shipped value points at an office OneDrive folder).
2. Workbook Setup S-41 and the template core-property version must equal CURRENT.json or the generator stops
   (`FAIL version gate`). A pre-v0.3 workbook is migrated with
   `"%DOCS_PY%" "<STANDARD>\build\patch_workbook_v03.py" <old.xlsx> <new.xlsx>`, never by hand; then register every
   existing calc (RECORD only if it was actually checked).
3. Never use `--allow-version-mismatch` for a job deliverable.

### B. Kickoff and folder (W00-W02)
4. Confirm the reviewing agency (City vs County) from the parcel record and the contract before drafting (HJR-C19);
   record the basis in Kickoff. Jurisdiction rules override this skill; load the `drainage-report-build` add-on.
5. Build the report folder with `make_report_folder.py` (command in `reference/governance_and_kickoff.md`), then add
   `30_Report\Issued\` beside `50_Correspondence\` and `00_Admin\DECISION_REGISTER.md` (D56, QC-C05; v0.3 does not
   create them). Dates in every folder and file name are YYYYMMDD (D56).
6. Fill Kickoff and Setup (S-01, S-03, S-04, S-06 flags, then the rest). Where the agency has a standard report
   outline (City of Tucson), its section list governs: keep every section and write "Intentionally left blank"
   with the reason where nothing applies; split existing conditions into hydrology and existing stormwater
   infrastructure (HJR-C19). In v0.3 do this with Narrative VERBATIM rows per section.
7. Set Setup S-36 to chapter-based numbering before any figure is rendered; figures and tables are numbered by
   section (Figure 4-1) (D52). Exhibit files `Fig<sec>-<n>_<Title>_<YYYYMMDD>.pdf`.
8. Plan: write `00_Admin\COORDINATION_PLAN.md` per the spec and seed CalcRegister / Narrative / ExhibitRegister
   (procedure and rules in `reference/governance_and_kickoff.md`). Stop for JCO approval of the plan.
9. Concept reports (channels with multi-use paths crossing roads, freeways or railroads; sites crossed by a large
   offsite wash) - put in the introduction, not deep in the body (HYD-C27):
   - whether the path is continuous under major crossings (freeway, railroad) or ends at them, and the crossing type
     at each road (at grade, under, con-arch);
   - for each existing crossing structure: stays, adequate, or replaced;
   - offsite conveyance alternatives with the count of road crossings for each; prefer one consolidated crossing;
     compare culvert cells for 10-yr vs 100-yr capacity;
   - alternatives note bank-protection options (e.g. geosynthetics on 4:1 vegetated slopes), precast vs
     cast-in-place culvert extensions, basin or spreader options at overchutes, terraced channel option (10-yr
     low-flow channel, 100-yr terrace outside sensitive areas);
   - flow paths described in downstream order;
   - written client decisions on level of protection (100-yr vs 500-yr), onsite containment and acceptance of
     controlled flooding; a designed overflow onto the site needs agency agreement;
   - grates/bar racks at fence crossings checked for headloss and debris; next deliverables listed after decisions.

### C. Governance during the work (W03-W05)
10. The ask creates the row: add the WORKING row before opening software. Work only in
    `20_Working\<Initials>_<YYYYMMDD>_<Topic>\`. Promote with `promote_calc.py` (OPTION, or RECORD with checker
    initials). Actions PROMOTE / CASCADE / QC-TABLE / RECONCILE / PRECHECK: `reference/governance_and_kickoff.md`.
11. Decision register (QC-C05): when two values exist for one feature (design flow, structure size, basis) across
    tables, workbook and plans, list each with source, method and where used; classify isolated vs propagating;
    resolve isolated, evidence-backed ones and log them; ask JCO propagating ones one at a time (problem, options,
    consequences, plan/profile image). No table edit until decided. Once decided, update narrative, tables, exhibit
    labels, HY-8 and protection sizing together; keep each native run. Log in `00_Admin\DECISION_REGISTER.md`.
12. Design discharge traceability (HJR-C10): define regional and local storms and their peaks once in existing
    conditions and use the qualifier with every reference (10-yr regional, 100-yr local), no synonyms; keep a design
    discharge table (source cross section or culvert record ID, location, Q10, Q100, governing duration, use:
    crossing vs parallel flow); use only the jurisdiction's design recurrence intervals; restate the basis in the
    design section with the same wording and numbers; check every caption and table title against the storm of the
    values shown; summary flow = flow used to size the structure; allowable velocity is the velocity permitted over a
    lining or soil. v0.3 has no T-HYD-10 block: keep the table as T-HYD-04 rows plus a Narrative VERBATIM table
    lead-in, or in 40_QC as the check list.
13. Appendix calc rules (HYD-C26, D16, D38, D30, EXH-C13):
    - once plans show a selected design, run that design (size, count, inverts, length from plans, project-datum
      inverts, not an arbitrary 100 ft datum) and insert native output; drop option-comparison tables. Options still
      open: native sheets for each option, not only a summary;
    - licensed set (D16, default, to confirm): FHWA Hydraulic Toolbox, HY-8, Civil 3D hydraulic tools, HEC-RAS,
      HEC-HMS, FLO-2D, PC-Hydro. FlowMaster and CulvertMaster are legacy: reproduce legacy calcs in Toolbox / HY-8;
    - no new spreadsheet a reviewer must check; independent checks stay in 40_QC (D30);
    - print areas set so every output sheet plots on one page;
    - native output always in the appendix; an extracted or compact sheet may be added, titled "extracted summary",
      every value traced to the native file (D38);
    - Hydraulic Toolbox inlets: do not tick Add Profile; keep the native Word export as evidence; compact one-inlet
      page filled only from saved .hyd values; where the export prints longitudinal slope 0.0000, show the saved slope
      with a note that the native export misprints it; check every compact page visually.
14. Fill table blocks from RECORD printouts only; units in headers; one software version per analysis per cycle.

### D. Recalculate (D51)
15. Every time a script wrote to the workbook (and before any assembly):
    `"%DOCS_PY%" "%SK%\xl_recalc.py" recalc --workbook "<wb>" --keep-copy "<wb>.pre_recalc.xlsx" --json "<..>\40_QC\recalc_<YYYYMMDD>.json"`
    Private Excel instance, events and link updates off, CalculateFullRebuild, then semantic compare. Require zero
    formula or input changes, zero new formula errors, and CalcRegister row-3 counters / Manifest J4 equal to what
    Excel shows. Work on an isolated workbook copy when testing; write only explicit input cells. Do not use the
    v0.3 `xl_recalc.ps1` (D12). LibreOffice recalc is a fallback only; flag it.

### E. Assemble (W06)
16. Run to a new dated file (issued drafts are never overwritten):
    ```
    "%DOCS_PY%" "<STANDARD>\standard\assemble_report.py" ^
      --workbook "<..>\00_Admin\<Job>_<ReportID>_Workbook.xlsx" ^
      --template "<STANDARD>\Psomas_Drainage_Report_TEMPLATE.docx" ^
      --out "<..>\30_Report\Drafts\<Job>_<ReportID>_<Milestone>_<YYYYMMDD>_DRAFT.docx"
    ```
    `VERSION GATE FAILED` -> stop and report.
17. Read `_ASSEMBLY_REPORT.md`:
    - s1 must show OK version gate, OK verbatim narrative present unchanged, OK no engineer notes / context-only text
      printed. FAIL on CalcRegister (duplicate RECORD, RECORD without checker) blocks issue.
    - Issue gate (QC-C04; v0.4 CS-04 automates it): QC_Log Tier 1 answered > 0; CalcRegister populated for a design
      report; zero unregistered figures (every `[FIGURE:F-nn]` has an ExhibitRegister row); s3 VERIFY citations
      checked (prior study citation, current ADEQ CGP edition); a table referenced in two sections has one owner.
    - s5 unresolved placeholders -> list for the engineer; they stay yellow in Word (D44).
    - s9 human decisions grouped: governance first (duplicate RECORD, RECORD without checker, table rows citing
      non-RECORD calcs, narrative on excluded sections, ReportText withheld), then Manifest, text, data, derivations.
    - s10a rewrites: fill `proposed` in `_REWRITES.json` for each item (same numbers, names, cited standards; section
      tone; no new facts); show original -> proposed; record Accept / Revert / Edit (`final`); then
      `"%DOCS_PY%" "<STANDARD>\standard\apply_rewrites.py" --docx <draft> --rewrites <..>\_REWRITES.json`.
      Accepted wording that should persist goes back into the Narrative cell as VERBATIM. Not reviewable until s10a
      is empty.
    - s11 = calculation-of-record list for the transmittal.
18. Open items (D44): one internal QC open-items document in 40_QC (prerequisites table: jurisdiction, plans match
    analysis, T2 check, seal, waivers, open items; numbered open items typed geotechnical / final design / waiver /
    approval / JCO decision / submittal; native-vs-report calc cross-check table; standards checklist with status and
    location, deviations called out; empty markup response log). Every assembly WARN, unresolved placeholder and
    human decision is closed or listed there. Checklist status uses Addressed / Partial / Assumed / Not Addressed /
    Cannot Determine / Stale (D45); rows resting on lidar culvert data, assumed bridge geometry, unknown layout or
    unconfirmed calibration are Partial or Assumed. Deviations from the Standard (tool version, exhibit method,
    missing template) are listed as JCO decisions. Deliverables read in completed tense; the open-items document is
    never transmitted.

### F. Post-process the DOCX
19. ```
    "%DOCS_PY%" "%SK%\postprocess_docx.py" --docx <draft.docx> --fix --out <draft>_PP.docx --preparer "Psomas (JCO)" --json <..>\40_QC\postprocess_<YYYYMMDD>.json
    ```
    Sets author / last-modified-by to the firm string, clears comments/keywords/subject, drops template custom
    properties, removes DATE fields from headers and footers. It lists, and never deletes, placeholders, leftover
    `[FIGURE:]` / `[TABLE:]` / `[LIB:]` slots and rewrite tags (D44: placeholders stay flagged until the assembly
    report shows them closed). Remove template paragraphs that do not apply and slots of excluded sections by hand
    or by regenerating; set cover office address and project number in Setup and regenerate.
20. Fix every finding at its source (workbook, Narrative, template), regenerate, and re-run. Tables: thin borders on
    all cells, header row in the template header style, no alternating shading (D47, default, to confirm); one
    caption per table above it, numbered by section, no second title inside the table; header row repeats; cells
    centered; portrait and full width (drop constant columns and note them); native Word tables, never screenshots;
    elevations 2 decimals without thousands separator, discharges whole cfs, one precision per column; each table
    introduced by a "presented in Table n" sentence; fit to one page where possible (RPT-C06).
    Page breaks only before main sections and appendices; template styles for headings and spacing, no manual
    returns; references numbered 1), 2) with real sources only; directions abbreviated with a period (S.) or road
    names written out, one convention; no dates in footers; fix TOC tab alignment and stray characters (pull a fresh
    template if unsure); cover carries a project site photo, preferably from the field visit (RPT-C06).
21. Figures embedded in the docx are downsampled to 200-300 dpi at print size before insertion.

### G. Word export
22. ```
    "%DOCS_PY%" "%SK%\word_export.py" --docx <draft>_PP.docx --pdf <..>\30_Report\Drafts\<name>.pdf --email-pdf <..>\<name>_email.pdf
    ```
    Separate Word instance; fields, TOC and tables of figures updated twice; PDF with heading bookmarks. Then
    confirm no paragraph lacks a named style and every Table/Figure number resolved (LibreOffice previews show
    "Table Introduction-1" where Word shows "Table 1-1": judge captions in Word).
23. Render every page and look at each one (`pdftoppm -r 45 -png <pdf> <prefix>`, contact sheets 5x2) before
    issue: cover on one page, footer not on 11x17 figure pages, no large white areas, no orphaned headings.

### H. Compile the bookmarked PDF (W09)
24. Write `30_Report\compile_manifest.json` (format in the script docstring) from the newest editable source and its
    fresh Word export: body split at the end of each main section with that section's 11x17 figures inserted, one
    divider per appendix and per plan set or study, native output (PC-Hydro printouts and hydrographs per CP, HEC-HMS
    output, Atlas 14 PFDS printout, HY-8 report, RAS computation summaries, FIS/LOMR/dam-safety pages), landscape
    pages rotated. Never hardcode page numbers in prose.
25. Prepare sources: highlight the relevant Q values in reference studies; replace table numbers on images with markup
    matching size, font and color; flatten author markups in the PDF reader (originals kept); third-party FreeText
    (e.g. LOMR pages) flattened or noted; inherited plan revision clouds removed from the compiled copy, original
    marked PDFs kept (D48).
26. ```
    "%DOCS_PY%" "%SK%\compile_pdf.py" build --manifest <..>\30_Report\compile_manifest.json --split
    ```
    Required bookmarks (D52, default, to confirm): cover, TOC, each main section, each appendix, each exhibit; children
    sorted by page. Checks: every bookmark and link target resolves, links dropped by the compile fail, page-by-page
    source comparison in the QA JSON (keep it in 40_QC), near-blank pages, size against S-35.1 / the agency limit
    (D52: 50 MB per file or the agency limit if lower; over -> compress, then split at top-level bookmarks; keep a
    reduced copy for transfer).
27. Placeholder pages only for named future items, labelled with the item; no blank areas in the body; remove
    unneeded pages, unrequested appendices and review-draft wording (D50).
28. Final interactive check of bookmarks and links in a native PDF reader (Bluebeam), not a browser viewer.
29. A pending model rerun: hand the watcher (wait for the new HDF, regenerate results and figures, recompile, copy to
    10_Record) to `model-run-supervisor`.

### I. Issue (W10) and after
30. Gate: open-items document empty, or JCO authorization recorded and the unresolved items listed in a separate
    internal document (D44); PRECHECK pass; RevisionLog row for the milestone; T1 complete, then T2 and T3.
31. Issued set in `30_Report\Issued\<YYYYMMDD>_<Milestone>\` with RECORD_SET.md (final PDF, frozen docx, transmittal).
    Handover package -> `delivery-package-build` (into 30_Report/Issued). Comments back -> `agency-comment-response`.
32. Design change after issue: log it in REVISION_LOG.md with affected letters, figures, tables and sections; CASCADE
    for hydrology changes; re-run in a new 20_Working folder; promote; regenerate to a new dated draft; compare old vs
    new drafts (Word Compare or `pandoc -t markdown` + diff) and the two assembly reports; T2 reopens for changed
    letters, T3 for changed sections; recompile.
33. Text that belongs in every future report goes into the library JSON (v0.4 release work), never into one .docx;
    project prose goes into Narrative or CalcRegister ReportText so regeneration reproduces it.

### J. End-to-end rerun of a job (DSO-C14)
34. Parameterize the project root and job work folder in every script (one parameter file); grep for absolute paths
    before a rerun - none outside the parameter file. Scripts write `.log` and `.err`; dated scripts folder
    `20_Working\<Initials>_<YYYYMMDD>_scripts\` (D56 replaces 99_Working).
35. Prerequisites: .hy8 writer module, minimal HMS template project, Report_Template_7 and memo template paths, pinned
    ras_commander, pywinauto, HY-8 8.00, HEC-HMS 4.13 (D01), HEC-RAS 6.6 (D02). Fix known blocking items from the
    prior run first.
36. Run order: due diligence; data/GIS (DEM, subbasins, culverts, terrain compare, crossings, inventory); hydrology
    (HMS build/runs, PC-Hydro, routing); 1D/2D runs in a separate agent; HY-8; alternatives; exhibits; report
    (recalc, assemble, post-process, Word export, contact sheets); compile; record copy. FLO-2D and HEC-RAS in
    parallel on separate core sets (D06 limits on EKOS).
37. Budget wall time: about 6.5 h for a one-session preliminary report; about 48 h minimum for a full 2D pilot,
    governed by HEC-RAS (10 plans about 43 h sequential on 12 cores); report build about 3 min per rebuild.
38. Every edit script is idempotent: back up first, check whether an insert already exists, assert counts before
    writing. After a JCO change edit the builder inputs first; do not run stale downstream builders.

## Jurisdiction add-ons
- Load `get_skill("drainage-report-build", resource="addons/<file>.md")` for the reviewing agency before step 6.
- `addons/city-of-tucson.md`: City manual outline is the section list (HJR-C19).
- `addons/town-of-marana.md`: concept reports explain trail termination or the crossing at I-10/UPRR (HYD-C27);
  regional vs local terminology per MDM 4.1 (HJR-C10, D24).
- `addons/town-of-sahuarita.md` / `addons/pima-county-rfcd.md`: a designed overflow onto the site conflicts with
  matching existing peak Q and floodplain at the property boundary (HYD-C27); 10-yr and 100-yr are the design events
  (HJR-C10).
- `addons/fema.md`: TDN behaviour via S-02.

## Gotchas
- openpyxl reads stale values for formula cells unless the workbook was recalculated and saved by Excel (SAH-012).
- A library-written workbook showed a COUNTIF wildcard counter of -14 status issues; native recalc gave 0 with no
  formula change (EKOS-LOCAL-018).
- Native Excel merges adjacent validation ranges and drops default styles; compare semantics, not raw XML
  (EKOS-LOCAL-018).
- Learning the workbook layout took four inspection passes plus manifest and library dumps; keep a named-range map per
  Standard version (SAH-012).
- Compiled PDF was 23.8 MB; a 3.4 MB compressed copy was needed for transfer (SAH-012).
- Figures first numbered 1-7, then renumbered by section, so every exhibit was rendered twice (CALFIRE-013).
- The memo template ships its own core.xml and duplicated parts (CALFIRE-013).
- TOC level-2 tab leader missing in the template on short entries (CALFIRE-013).
- Cover office address and project number were placeholders (CALFIRE-013).
- Generated DOCX was 49
